### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A25, A26, A31, A32 and A33 each occurred exactly once per trace (mean 1.0, no repeats). In the later window, each occurs on average about 3.06 times per trace, and about 66.5% of traces contain repeated occurrences. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- In the earlier window, A33 was always followed by A20. In the later window, about 67% of A33's outgoing transitions go to A25, and about 33% still go to A20. [DIR001]
- In the earlier window, A25, A26, A31, A32 and A33 appeared in a fixed order relative to each other and to A23: for example, A25 always preceded A26/A31/A32/A33, and A23 always followed them. In the later window, these pairs are interleaved or repeated in about 66.5% of traces, with the fixed order remaining in only about 33.5%. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- A17 was present in 55.5% of traces in the earlier window and always occurred after A25/A26/A31/A32/A33. In the later window it is present in 46% of traces, and in about 27.5% of traces it is interleaved with those activities instead of strictly following them. Its mean position also shifted later, from about 0.65 to 0.72 of the trace. [POS001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- A23 shifted later in the trace (mean position from about 0.70 to 0.76), and its relation with A25/A26/A31/A32/A33 changed from always following them to being interleaved in about 66.5% of traces. [POS002, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- The distance between A26, A31 and A32 increased: in the earlier window they were almost always 1–2 steps apart (about 64–69% at lag 1 and 30–36% at lag 2); in the later window they are spread over lags 1–5, with only about 10–13% at lag 1. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a hypothesis that the segment involving A25, A26, A31, A32 and A33 changed from a single pass through a fixed sequence to a repeated, interleaved execution, with A33 sometimes looping back to A25. In the earlier window these activities occurred once per trace in a fixed order; in the later window they repeat about three times per trace, are interleaved in about two-thirds of traces, and A33 is followed by A25 in about two-thirds of its transitions. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR001, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006]

Other differences: A17 became less frequent and shifted later, and A23 shifted later; these are consistent with the same reordering but could reflect a separate change in participation or placement. [POS001, POS002, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]

The screening comparison strongly exceeds chance expectation (39 control-flow items versus 0.51 expected), so the overall pattern is unlikely to be a sampling artefact. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the decline of A17 is an independent change rather than part of the same reordering. [screening.by_family]
